points.en: yellowish-buff supercilium, strongest above and behind the eye and weaker in front of it

art.subject: Buff-throated Warbler (Phylloscopus subaffinis), adult (sexes alike): upperparts plain dull olive-brown; a yellowish-buff supercilium, weaker and less contrasting than in Tickell's Leaf Warbler; a dusky eye-stripe; underparts dull yellow strongly washed buff, most ochraceous on the throat, breast and flanks; no wing-bars; plain dark olive-brown wings and tail; small, fine bill, dark with a pale yellowish base to the lower mandible; dark eye; pale pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched low in a dense shrub, side view
art.scene: shrubby hillside scrub with tall grasses on a Korean offshore island during spring migration in May, soft light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched low in a dense shrub: small, compact leaf warbler, plain olive-brown upperparts, yellowish-buff supercilium strongest above and behind the eye and fading in front of it, short largely dark bill, plain wings without wing-bars, dull yellowish underparts washed buff on the throat, breast and flanks, square tail

adult, front three-quarter view perched on a grass stem: yellowish-buff supercilium, buff-washed yellowish throat and breast, brownish-buff flanks, plain olive-brown wings without bars, short largely dark bill
art.build: A small, plain leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow and close to a Dusky Warbler in size, rather compact with a rounded head and a medium-length square tail. Bill fine and short, much shorter than the head. Legs slender. Wings short and rounded, with no bars. Keeps low in scrub and tall grass rather than high in trees.
avoid: Do not add wing-bars, a crown stripe or a pale rump.
Do not paint whitish underparts; that would be Dusky Warbler (Phylloscopus fuscatus). This species is buffy-yellow below.
Do not paint bright lemon-yellow underparts with bright green upperparts.
